programmes.d: A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.
In 1996, Virginia Beach police arrive at the Makdessi apartment to find the bloodied bodies of Elise Makdessi and Navy sailor Quincy Brown. But was Brown Elise's lover or her assailant?
A college student was found dead, and the evidence suggested he knew his killer.
Armed with little else, police hoped that shoe impressions found at a Lansing, Michigan crime scene would put their investigation of Audrey Nichols' murder back on track.
In this classic episode of Forensic Files, the longest-running true crime series in television history, a serial bomber targets a judge, two attorneys and even a courthouse.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a murder crime scene.
A police officer accused of killing his estranged wife insists she committed suicide.
When court clerk Peter Porco doesn't report to work in November 2004, a courts officer is ordered to the Porcos' family home in Bethlehem, NY.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.
A young woman is stabbed more than 100 times. The killer leaves DNA behind, but investigators must play a cat-and-mouse game to obtain a suspect's DNA to match.
The difficulty in solving bombings.

When convenience store employee Wanda Mason is found dead, investigators find the entire murder has been caught on the store's security camera. But the image of the killer is so degraded it seems impossible to positively identify him.
Pathologist examining death of politician running for re-election finds puncture wounds at autopsy.

A young couple decided to celebrate their first wedding anniversary with a camping trip to Mount Hood. During the trip, the husband was shot and killed. Later, his wife told two different versions of the events which led to his death.
A man denies killing a pedestrian in a hit-and-run, claiming he sold the car in question.

Casino security cameras tracked a young woman's movements until shortly before she disappeared. She was never seen again, but through the evidence she left behind, she was able to tell investigators what happened to her and who was responsible.
Two men were murdered and investigators find a link to an arson.
Two sets of scientists probe a woman's death.
A young woman attends evening church services... then disappears.

When an elderly couple died in a suspicious house fire, their son became the prime suspect. Investigators turned to forensic science to determine if the fire had been set deliberately, or if it was an unfortunate accident.
Arsenic poisoning is found to be the cause of a woman's mysterious illness.
A highway patrolman was dispatched to what he thought would be a routine traffic accident — until he looked in the car. He had seen hundreds of accidents, but none with as much blood as this.
When a hit-and-run accident killed a high school athlete, everyone in town searched for the killer.
Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon in April 2002 after he planned to end their relationship.
Chilling tale of debt and deceit when the head chef of a restaurant is found dead.

In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with one of her sons, her granddaughter and $500,000 in gold coins. The police investigated several suspects, including David R. Waters, who worked for American Atheists.
In 1989, 4-year-old April Loveless was found dead in the backyard of her Texas home.
When 19-year-old Lori Auker left her Pennsylvania home for work and never arrived, it took space-age technology, cat hairs and insects to pinpoint the woman's abductor.
An 18-month-old skeleton found on marshland puts forensics to the ultimate test.

When police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife, authorities linked 20 cat hairs found on her jacket to a cat owned by Beamish's parents. It was the first time animal DNA was used to solve a criminal case.
After a man dies in a fire, his death is ruled an accident until forensic science is used.
Authorities track a kidnapper who let his victim write a last will and informed the family of her murder. A phone number written on a previous page left a lasting impression, which helped to convict.
In 1995, Palm Beach waitress Denise O'Neill is abducted and murdered.
In 2008, college co-ed Jenna Verhaalen was found dead in her Bryan, Texas apartment. Petechial hemorrhages in her eyes indicated that she was strangled.
In 2007, Brian & Beverly Mauck were found dead in their Graham, Washington home.
The victim was well liked and successful, which made the brutality of the crime even harder to understand.
When police find the body of an 11-year-old, there are few clues to the killer's identity.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas. Later, a fourth murder from the same time period provided the police with far more than they realized.
In 2008, college co-ed Jenna Verhaalen was found dead in her Bryan, Texas apartment.

A killer tries to incinerate everything that could link him to his crime. But in doing so, he inadvertently creates new forensic evidence. Detectives employ a technique never before used in a criminal investigation to bring it to light.
In 1993, Rose Larner stopped in a convenience store and was never seen or heard from again.
A 1995 fire razes the mansion of a Kansas doctor, killing two of her three children.
A Michigan State University grad student disappeared and was presumed dead. With the help of a professor of geological sciences, police hoped to get the "dirt" on her killer.
Old-fashioned police work and computer animation determine how a 15-year-old boy was shot.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers. An investigator reveals that their ill health is due to mold in their modern home.
A husband and wife get shot, and their 16-year-old daughter manages to escape.

The wife of an Air Force officer was found dead in her bed with a plastic laundry bag near her face. Further investigation proved that the scene had been staged. Her death wasn't an accident — it was cold-blooded murder.
The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage.
A Colorado hunter is the victim of a well-planned crime. Investigators suspect two weapons and two killers. But forensic evidence points them in a different direction — one much closer to home.
The kidnapping of Adolph Coors leads to one of the most intense manhunts in US history.
It was a tragic twist of fate. Just days after a woman sold her home and moved to a modest trailer, a fire took both the trailer and her life. But the autopsy proved this was no accident.
With the use of DNA profiling, an innocent man is freed and the real killer is convicted.

On a cold December night in 1993, Rose Larner stopped in a convenience store on her way to her boyfriend's house. She was never seen or heard from again. Rose's disappearance remained a mystery, until a tiny clue is found years later.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause millions of dollars worth of damage and the deaths of three people. He is discovered, partly through the use of forensic hypnosis.
More than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984.
When a nine-year-old girl goes missing, police and volunteers spend weeks searching for her.

A go-go dancer told her family she needed to get away for a while and then she simply disappeared. Investigators were suspicious, because she took neither her car nor her clothes. 20 years later, her family received a call that changed everything.
California police had several suspects in the robbery and brutal murder of an elderly couple.
When Chris Ochoa confessed to the 1988 rape and murder of Nancy DePriest, the case was closed. 8 years later, Achim Marino confessed to the same crime. Can DNA evidence identify the real perpetrator?
When two women from the same town were murdered, police feared a serial killer was on the loose.
In 1997, Kelly Eckart's car was found, with her belongings still in it, after she worked a late shift in Franklin, Indiana. Days later, her body was found in an isolated ravine.
The victim has been stabbed more than thirty times, and the crime scene is awash with her blood.
A 13-year-old girl went missing from her Colorado home. The only evidence the kidnapper left behind was three fingerprints on a window screen.
A man is murdered in his sleep, no fingerprints are left, a shoe impression leads to the killer.

In 1984, California firefighters battled ten arson fires in three weeks. When cigarettes and a scrap of paper connected the case to similar fires further north, the hunt was on for a dangerous pyromaniac.
In a rich suburb of Philadelphia, police were called to what appeared to be an accidental drowning.

A young woman is found dead in her apartment. With little evidence at the scene, the case turns cold — until police discover a link between their prime suspect and an unsolved murder committed six years earlier in a different state.
In rural Canada, a doctor is accused of sedating and sexually assaulting a female patient.

The victim had been sexually assaulted and stabbed to death on the beach. A pair of men's tennis shoes was discovered near her body. Police were sure that if they found the man who fit the shoes, they would also find the man who committed the crime.
A victim's knowledge of forensic evidence leads police to her abductor.

Alaskan hikers discover a body wrapped in sheets which were edged in orange stitching. Investigators find a tuft of red carpet fibers clinging to the sheet — threads of evidence which lead them straight to the killer.
Haunted by the disappearance of her mother, a young woman undertakes an investigation of her own.
Who was the sexual offender who murdered two adolescent boys in Nebraska? The key to stopping him would be the unique composition of the "junk rope" he used to tie his victims.
When a policeman's house goes up in flames, experts suspect arson. But then the suspect vanishes.
When a pipe bomb rips through a rural home, police have no idea who is responsible. A 9-volt battery and the remnants of a mailing label ead investigators to the man who made the bomb.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a boy scout camp near Farmington, Missouri.
In 2005, David Castor suffered a slow, agonizing death over a period of days. His wife maintained it was suicide, even though it was done with antifreeze.
A woman dies after a long search for medical help in dealing with the side effects of lithium.

In 1993, the Amtrak Railroad experienced the deadliest train crash in United States history when the Sunset Limited derailed while crossing Alabama's Big Bayou Canot bridge. 47 passengers and crew were killed; scores more were injured.
In 1993, Rose Larner stopped in a convenience store and was never seen or heard from again.
When Rosemary Anderson is found dead on the side of the road, her boyfriend becomes the prime suspect. He eventually confessed to her murder, but so did another man: serial killer Eric Edgar Cooke.
A woman disappears without a trace. Even though foul play is suspected, the leads don't pan out.
In 1989, the dead bodies of Joan Rogers and her two teenage daughters were found floating in Tampa Bay.
A woman is found dead in a ravine, but crucial crime scene evidence had been washed away by storms.
Foul play is suspected when Fort Worth factory worker Glenda Furch disappears after completing her shift.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine.
A surgeon is stabbed to death and the most likely suspect is seen in a restaurant at the time of the murder.
A beverage company pleads guilty to violating federal safety laws when a baby dies from E. coli.

Police are led on a wild goose chase when the wife of a prominent banker is kidnapped. An entomologist's unexpected discovery leads to a new suspect — and the realization that ordinary office equipment can leave extraordinary clues.
A 16-year-old girl is killed in her own home by her parents, who claim they acted in self-defense.

The disappearance of Philadelphia college athlete Aimee Willard is investigated after her car is found on the roadside. When her body is found, the police find unusual marks and DNA evidence that eventually lead to her killer.
Distinctive boots and a sweet tooth leads investigators to the killer of a WWII veteran.
Evidence suggests the suspect of an unusual robbery-homicide case ran out of the house and not in.
Soon after becoming pregnant by Dr. Maynard Muntzing, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates. Eventually, she raises suspicions that Muntzing is doing her harm.
Fire wood found at a crime scene helps investigators locate a killer.

A woman appears to have lost control of her SUV and plunged down an embankment into a shallow creek. But investigators suspect foul play when they find snowy footprints leading away from the crime scene.
Arsenic poisoning is found to be the cause of a woman's mysterious illness.

A police officer accused of killing his estranged wife insists she committed suicide. Investigators say it was murder — that it was physically impossible for the woman to have shot herself.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.

When the decomposed body of a teenage girl is discovered, police have no clues to her identity. To solve the case, investigators turn to bug larvae found on the body and a tiny wad of chewing gum found near the victim's body.
